```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment="#>",fig.width=6,fig.height=4)
library("coherent4cast")
```

## Define the history and the question

The package takes one row per observed counting-process interval. A subject can
have recurrent events until one absorbing terminal event. `event_type = 0`
means that no recurrent event was observed at the interval end; it does not mean
that an unmonitored interval was event free. Every analysis declares a time unit.

```{r data}
data("sim_perinatal")
head(sim_perinatal)
trajectory <- as_trajectory(sim_perinatal, event_types=c("1","2"),
                            time_unit="months")
history <- build_history(trajectory, cap=2)
head(history$counts)
```

These data are simulated. The domain label demonstrates data organization; it
does not establish a maternal-health risk model. Counts used as intensity
features are capped at two, while predicted event burden continues to count
events occurring after the cap.

## Fit one event-history law

```{r fit}
fit <- coherent4cast(~x, sim_perinatal, event_types=c("1","2"),
                time_unit="months")
print(fit)
glance(fit)
head(tidy(fit))
```

Each event type and the terminal event has a separate baseline, covariate
coefficient and history dependence. A shared mean-one gamma frailty induces
dependence. Analytic gamma integration produces subject scores and information;
the covariance estimate clusters contributions by independent subject.
Inspect `fit$convergence` before using regular Wald inference. A boundary or
nonpositive-information fit remains visibly flagged.

## Forecast at an explicit landmark

```{r predict}
one <- sim_perinatal[sim_perinatal$id == 1, ]
forecast <- predict(fit, newdata=one, landmark=0,
                    horizon=c(.25,.5,1), type="all")
forecast[, c("unit","horizon","target","estimate")]
plot(forecast, target="risk")
```

`risk` is terminal-event probability; `survival` is its complement. `burden_1`
and `burden_2` are expected additional counts stopped by the terminal event.
`rmst` is expected time alive within the forecast horizon. The fitted law
produces all these quantities. Future rows are not used as landmark history.
Measured covariates are held at their landmark values during this forecast.

The output reports uniformization series error separately from floating-point
probability error. Neither is a bound on gamma quadrature error. Compare
quadrature resolutions when a mixture forecast is sensitive to numerical
integration.

```{r quadrature}
q15 <- predict(fit, one, landmark=0, horizon=1, quadrature=15)
q30 <- predict(fit, one, landmark=0, horizon=1, quadrature=30)
abs(q15$estimate-q30$estimate)
```

## Reproduce and inspect assumptions

```{r audit}
fit$audit$assumptions
fit$audit$data_hash_algorithm
attr(forecast,"assumptions")
```

An integrity fingerprint helps detect changed inputs; it does not establish
correct observation assumptions. Predictions are prognostic quantities, not
treatment effects. Complete histories, rounded dates and unrecorded intervals
require distinct observation specifications.
